description:
Emit the prediction world (2026-10-10): a graded, closed world in which to
demonstrate ENDEMIC self-improvement -- the agent improving itself from its
own operation, judged by its own criterion, with an off arm.

The world (domains/prediction_world.py, mechanical): bodies move in a box;
each frame the agent observes their positions and its PREDICTOR -- graph
rules -- predicts where each will be next. Its criterion is its own surprise:
the distance between where it predicted a body would be and where it was.
Levels get harder: 1 drift (constant velocity), 2 bounce (walls), 3 fall
(gravity), 4 glide (damping), 5 bounce under gravity.

seeds/prediction_world.json (skippable; the part the agent changes)
  * Six base models, rank k = form_index*2 + reflect: velocity (x + dx),
    acceleration (x + 2dx - pdx: a constant change in displacement) or ratio
    (x + dx*dx/pdx: a constant ratio of displacements), each with or without
    `reflect` (fold a prediction that leaves the box back in).
  * Predictor{mask, model}: the agent's held model -- the set of base models
    it composes (bit k). One bit is a base model; more is a composite that
    uses, per body and axis, whichever component predicted that body best
    last frame (1.1.0).
  * PredictorCandidate{mask, name, rank, authored}: the models the agent may
    try, in MDL order. The six base models and the composition operator are
    human-written; which model to try, when, which composites to author, and
    whether to keep one is the agent's.
  * predict_body_next: the predictor itself.

seeds/prediction_self_improvement.json (frozen; the loop -- the agent may not
change how it judges itself)
  * PredictionCurriculum{current_level, max_level, last_change_seq} and
    PredictionPolicy{self_improvement, surprise_floor, window, min_gain,
    min_abs_gain}.
  * pw_advance_level: `window` consecutive episodes at the level at or under
    the floor -> the next level.
  * pw_file_surprise_concern: `window` episodes since the predictor last
    changed and the level not mastered -> SelfConcern{kind:'prediction_surprise'}.
    Endemic: nothing but the agent's own surprise files it.
  * pw_propose_predictor_edit: an open concern, self-improvement on -> one
    Experiment + SeedDelta per candidate not yet tried against the current
    model for this concern.
  * pw_concern_exhausted: no candidate left -> the concern says so.
  * pw_author_composite_predictor (1.1.0): an exhausted concern whose best
    local trial cleared the bar at the level and was refuted only on its
    retention cost -> the agent authors a new candidate, its current model
    composed with that winner, and reopens the concern. Composites compose
    further; one it already holds is not re-authored, so it terminates.
  * pw_request_residual_fit / pw_author_context_layer (1.2.0): an exhausted
    concern with nothing to compose -> the agent asks where its own model's
    surprise lives (ResidualFit: per context atom, the summed error of the
    frames where it holds, and the least-squares fit of those frames,
    x' - x = c0*dx + c1*pdx + c2*ppdx + c3, written by the mechanical
    half as ResidualCells); it then authors its current model plus a layer on
    the atom holding the most residual where the fit helps, and reopens the
    concern. The context atoms (reversal: dx*pdx < 0; after_reversal:
    pdx*ppdx < 0) and the linear layer form are human-written; which atom,
    the coefficients (from its own episodes), and whether to keep it are not.
  * pw_master_last_level (1.2.0): the last level is mastered like the others.
  * PredictionPolicy.authoring (1.2.0): 0 switches both authoring rules off
    (the no_authoring ablation).
  * Revision (1.3.0): residual fits also cover layers the model holds
    (refit one, or refit_all), each fit offered on the level alone and pooled
    with the mastered levels, one candidate per helpful fit;
    pw_author_pruned_component (the model minus one base component) and
    pw_author_dropped_layer (minus its last layer); layers gain a fifth term,
    the body's running acceleration estimate on the axis.
  * Robust mastery (1.4.0): the one-sided 95% upper confidence bound of the
    mean surprise of the last `mastery_window` (5) episodes under the current
    model at or under the floor; concerns filed on the mean of the last
    `window` episodes since the change, or after 2*mastery_window episodes
    without robust mastery.
  * Meta search (1.4.0): PredictionOperatorStat per authoring operator
    (tried / supported / adopted, updated by pw_count_operator_trial and
    pw_count_operator_adoption); with meta_search on, trials go in batches by
    operator yield (supported+1)/(tried+2), best first, and an operator tried
    meta_min_trials times with yield under meta_min_yield is skipped.
  * 1.5.0: experts (up to N_EXPERTS more full models on the Predictor, gated
    per body and axis by cumulative error; authored by pw_author_expert from
    the local winner and pw_author_specialist_expert from a level-only fit,
    both only once a concern's single-model fits are spent); provenance
    credit (`enabled`) in the operator record, and skipping only as a last
    resort; self-proposed policy changes (MetaProposal from META_GRAMMAR,
    measured on the agent's own practice levels by the mechanical half,
    judged and adopted by pw_judge_policy_change / pw_adopt_policy_change_*).
  * 1.6.0: the operator record per kind of world (box / open, read from the
    level's latest episode); skipping a real skip again (skip_last_resort 0);
    policy proposals in rounds (meta_round / meta_max_rounds, closed by
    pw_close_policy_round), supported only when they win on more practice
    levels than they lose.
  * 1.7.0: three judges for policy changes (net / sign / tail); with
    meta_calibrate on, round 0 is also measured on a second practice set and
    pw_select_policy_judge adopts the judge whose choice realised the most
    net there (ties: the stricter); later rounds use it.
  * 1.8.0: practice shaping -- with practice_shaping on, the agent screens a
    pool of candidate practice levels with its round's proposals and
    pw_select_practice_level keeps the practice_k where they disagree most.
  * 1.9.0: a layer on a predicate the agent authors itself (comb(F[a], F[b])
    < or > thr over observable features, found by its residual search and
    authored by pw_author_predicate_layer as a last resort); an escalating
    curriculum option (level_patience: move on from an unmastered level).
  * pw_judge_predictor_edit: the replay's variant surprise against its control
    surprise, on the agent's own recorded episodes at the level AND on its
    recorded episodes of the levels it has already mastered (retention):
    supported only when it is lower at the level by min_gain (relative) and
    its gain, net of retention_weight x the surprise it adds on mastered
    levels (summed per level, so one level's regression is neither diluted nor
    traded against another's improvement), reaches min_abs_gain. Weighed,
    not vetoed.
  * pw_adopt_predictor_edit: once every trial is judged, the supported trial
    with the best weighed net (ties: the simpler model) is adopted in the
    graph -- the Predictor takes the candidate's form -- and the concern is
    resolved.
Idempotent.

attrs.name: prediction_policy
attrs.description: The agent's own bar: mean surprise per body-frame (cells) at or under the floor masters a level; a model must cut it by 20%, and by 0.05 cells net of any surprise it adds on the levels already mastered, to be adopted.

rules.name: pw_advance_level
rules.comment: The level is mastered (1.4.0: robustly -- the upper confidence bound of the mean surprise of the last `mastery_window` episodes under the current model at or under the floor).

rules.name: pw_master_last_level
rules.comment: The last level is mastered the same way; there is nowhere to advance to.

rules.name: pw_move_on_from_level
rules.comment: 1.9.0: an escalating curriculum (level_patience > 0) does not wait forever: after level_patience episodes at a level not mastered, the agent moves on to the next one (its concern there stays).

rules.name: pw_file_surprise_concern
rules.comment: Endemic supply: `window` episodes since the predictor last changed and the level still not mastered (its last `window` episodes not all at or under the floor) files the agent's own concern. Nothing but its surprise decides this. (1.2.0: was 'none under the floor', which one lucky episode blocked forever.)

parts.value: my predictions keep missing at level

rules.name: pw_propose_predictor_edit
rules.comment: The agent's own trials for its concern: every candidate model it has not yet tried against its current one, each in its own experiment, so the alternatives are weighed against each other. 1.4.0: with meta_search on, in batches by the yield of the operator that authored each candidate (its own record), best first.

rules.name: pw_concern_exhausted
rules.comment: Every candidate model has been tried against the current one and none was supported: the concern says so honestly.

rules.name: pw_author_composite_predictor
rules.comment: An exhausted concern whose best local trial was refuted only on its retention cost: the agent authors a new model -- its current model and that winner, composed (per body and axis, whichever component predicted best last frame) -- adds it to its own candidate space and reopens the concern to try it. Composites compose further; a composite it already holds is not re-authored, so the concern stays exhausted when composition has nothing new to offer.

rules.name: pw_request_residual_fit
rules.comment: An exhausted concern with nothing left to compose (no local winner, or its composite is already held): the agent asks where its own model's surprise lives -- its residual on its own recorded episodes at the level, per context atom, both for atoms it does not yet condition on and for the layers it already holds (1.3.0: so it can revise what it built).

rules.name: pw_author_context_layer
rules.comment: The agent authors new models from its own residual, one per ResidualCell where the fit helps: its current model with a NEW context layer on an atom it does not yet use, or (1.3.0) with one of its own layers REFITTED; each fitted on the level's frames alone or pooled with the levels it has mastered. It reopens the concern, and the judge weighs the alternatives against each other. A model it already holds is not re-authored.

rules.name: pw_author_pruned_component
rules.comment: Revision (1.3.0): an exhausted concern with nothing to compose -- the agent authors its current model with one of its base components removed (its layers kept), one candidate per component, and reopens the concern; the judge weighs them like any other. A model it already holds is not re-authored.

rules.name: pw_author_dropped_layer
rules.comment: Revision (1.3.0): an exhausted concern with nothing to compose and a model with layers -- the agent authors its current model without its last layer, and reopens the concern.

rules.name: pw_author_expert
rules.comment: 1.5.0: scope-confined change. A concern whose best local trial cleared the bar at the level but was refuted on its retention cost: the agent authors its current model plus that winner as an EXPERT in a free slot -- per body and axis, the expert whose last prediction was best predicts -- so the specialist mostly acts only where it fits. The judge weighs it like any other candidate.

rules.name: pw_author_specialist_expert
rules.comment: 1.5.0: scope-confined change. From a ResidualFit's specialist cell -- its own base components with both context layers fitted from scratch on this level's frames alone -- the agent authors its current model plus that specialist as an expert in a free slot; per body and axis the expert whose last prediction was best predicts, so the specialist mostly acts only where it fits.

rules.name: pw_author_predicate_layer
rules.comment: 1.9.0: from a ResidualFit's author_atom cell -- a predicate over its observable features that the agent's own residual search found, and a layer fitted on its frames -- the agent authors its current model with that predicate layer (replacing any it held), and reopens the concern.

rules.name: pw_judge_predictor_edit
rules.comment: The agent's own criterion on its own recorded episodes, weighed: the variant must lower surprise at the level by min_gain (relative), and its gain, net of any surprise it adds on levels already mastered (retention_weight), must reach min_abs_gain.

rules.name: pw_adopt_predictor_edit
rules.comment: Once every trial is judged, the best supported trade is adopted in the graph: the Predictor takes the candidate model, the concern is resolved, and the episodes since are counted afresh.

rules.name: pw_count_operator_trial
rules.comment: The agent's record of its own search: a judged trial counts against the operator that authored its candidate (tried, and supported if the judge supported it).

rules.name: pw_count_operator_enabled
rules.comment: 1.5.0: a supported trial of a candidate authored from another operator's trial credits that operator too -- its trials are what the authoring built on.

rules.name: pw_count_operator_adoption
rules.comment: An adopted trial also counts as an adoption for its operator.

rules.name: pw_propose_policy_change
rules.comment: 1.5.0: with its curriculum mastered and meta_proposals on, the agent proposes changes to its own search policy -- each a MetaProposal the mechanical half measures on practice levels.

rules.name: pw_judge_policy_change
rules.comment: 1.5.0: a measured policy change, weighed: practice surprise plus retention harm saved, plus experiment_cost per experiment saved; supported when the net reaches meta_min_net and (1.6.0) the change wins on more practice levels than it loses, so no one level carries it.

rules.name: pw_select_policy_judge
rules.comment: 1.7.0: with meta_calibrate on, once round 0 is judged on its first practice set and measured on its second, the agent adopts the judge whose best supported proposal realised the most net on the second set (ties: the stricter). It uses that judge from then on.

rules.name: pw_adopt_policy_change_meta_min_trials
rules.comment: 1.5.0: once every proposal is judged, the best supported one is adopted (here: meta_min_trials).

rules.name: pw_adopt_policy_change_meta_min_yield
rules.comment: 1.5.0: once every proposal is judged, the best supported one is adopted (here: meta_min_yield).

rules.name: pw_adopt_policy_change_min_gain
rules.comment: 1.5.0: once every proposal is judged, the best supported one is adopted (here: min_gain).

rules.name: pw_adopt_policy_change_retention_weight
rules.comment: 1.5.0: once every proposal is judged, the best supported one is adopted (here: retention_weight).

rules.name: pw_close_policy_round
rules.comment: 1.6.0: a round of policy proposals closes once every proposal in it is judged and its best supported one (if any) is adopted; the next round proposes from the policy as it now stands.

rules.name: pw_select_practice_level
rules.comment: 1.8.0: once every candidate practice level of a pool is screened, the agent selects the practice_k with the largest spread of cost across its proposals (ties: the earlier candidate).
